subject: Proposal to Narrow Customer Indemnity for Model-Training IP Claims
messages:
From: Sara Mills <sara.mills@acmesoftware.com>

Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: carveout for model training IP claims / MSA redlines

Jonas / Redwood team —

Thanks for the updated MSA & order form. Our legal team flagged the broad customer indemnity around third-party IP claims tied to model training data. Specifically, they are asking us to: 1) limit customer indemnity exposure where claims arise from Customer-provided training data that they have licensed, and 2) carve out a narrow reverse-indemnity where Redwood’s model training process (e.g., use of open training pipelines) is the primary cause.

Attached are redlines from our counsel (acme_indemnity_redlines_20270509.pdf) showing the requested changes. High-level asks: 
- Remove "Customer shall indemnify for any claim related to data used to train models" language and replace with a requirement that Customer only indemnifies for claims arising from Customer-borne content that is not licensed appropriately.
- Add a mutual cooperation/evidence clause specific to training datasets and retain a 30-day cure window before indemnity obligations kick in.

We understand Redwood's position on protecting the model IP and want to propose a compromise that protects both parties. Can you share Redwood’s preferred fallback language and any proposed limits (cap, notice timing, control over defense)?

Best,

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: carveout for model training IP claims / MSA redlines

Jonas / Marissa — quick legal take and proposed language below. High-level risk view: Acme’s ask reduces our ability to shift risk for third-party claims tied to customer-supplied training data. We can accept a limited carveout provided we preserve (i) notice + cooperation and (ii) our ability to seek indemnity from third parties responsible for the claim. Recommend we also retain control of defense for claims that could materially implicate our model IP. 

Proposed compromise clause (sendable to Acme):
"
Customer Indemnity Limited to Customer Content. Customer shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Redwood Inference from and against any claim, suit or proceeding (and any resulting loss, liability or expense) to the extent arising out of Customer Content used by Redwood for model training where (a) Customer has failed to obtain rights to permit such use, and (b) the claim directly alleges infringement or misappropriation of a third party's intellectual property by such Customer Content. Redwood will provide notice of any claim, and Customer will have a 30-day period to cure or obtain a license. If Customer does not timely cure, Redwood may elect to control the defense; Redwood will use reasonable efforts to consult with Customer on material defense decisions. For clarity, this section does not limit Redwood's rights to seek indemnity or damages from any third party responsible for the claim.
"

Controls and limits we should propose: 
- Liability cap tied to the order form or a per-claim cap (we suggest a per-claim cap equal to the total fees paid in the prior 12 months for the applicable Order Form).
- We keep the right to control the defense for any claim that could reasonably affect Redwood’s model weights, training pipelines, or roadmap.
- Preservation of Redwood’s ability to assert third-party claims and seek contributions.

I’m attaching a doc with the clause (rdw_proposed_clause_20270510.docx). If you want to be more commercial and move faster, we can offer defense control but limit the damages cap to fees paid in prior 12 months. If Acme insists on mutual defense control, we should push for a carve-in where Redwood retains control if the claim would materially affect model IP.

Let me know if you want me to send the clause directly to Sara and propose the cap.

Sara — thanks for sharing the redlines and for outlining your position. We reviewed with legal and propose the attached compromise language (see text below). In short: we can narrow the Customer indemnity to Customer Content that is not licensed for training, preserve a 30-day cure window, and agree to reasonable cooperation — provided we retain the right to control defense when the claim implicates Redwood’s model weights or training pipelines. We also propose the liability cap be the fees paid under the Order Form in the prior 12 months (standard for this tier).

Proposed short paragraph for insertion into the MSA: 
"Customer Indemnity Limited to Customer Content and Cure Period: Customer shall indemnify Redwood for third-party claims to the extent such claims arise from Customer Content used in training when Customer failed to secure the necessary rights. Redwood shall provide notice and Customer shall have 30 days to cure or obtain a license. If Customer does not timely cure, Redwood may assume defense control for claims that would materially affect its model or training processes. Liability for such indemnified claims shall be capped at fees paid under the applicable Order Form in the prior 12 months.
"

If that sounds workable, Kim can circulate a tracked version and we’ll propose a short call to finalize. We can also include a fallback where Acme controls defense for consumer-facing claims that clearly do not touch our model IP.

Would Friday EOD work for you to finalize? I’ll include the DocuSign link and a clean MSA/order form once we align.

Thanks —
